title: Self-review not prevented — reviewer picker populates from all project members without excluding the policy owner or `createdBy`; author can self-approve; no server-side validation; violates Annex A 5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** Reviewer dropdown populated from all `orgMembers` without filtering out the policy's `createdBy` or `owner`. `submitForReview` backend accepts any valid ObjectId as `reviewerId` without checking for self-assignment.
**Impact:** Authors can approve their own work. ISO 27001 Annex A 5.3 (separation of duties) violated. Auditor sampling approved policies may find the author and approver are the same person.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Frontend: `const eligibleReviewers = orgMembers.filter(m => m._id !== policy.createdBy && m._id !== policy.owner);`. Backend `submitForReview`: `if (String(reviewerId) === String(policy.createdBy)) return res.status(400).json({error: 'Policy author cannot be the reviewer'});`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The architecture moved: reviewer assignment is no longer done from `PolicyEdit.jsx` — it now happens via an 'Assign Reviewer' modal in `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyDetailView.jsx` (reviewForm state ~line 307, modal ~line 2460-2484), backed by the `useProjectMembers` hook (`vibrantix-client-panel/src/hooks/useProjectMembers.js`). Re-verified 2026-08-27: `useProjectMembers.js` builds its `options` list purely from `GET /projects/project/:id/team` (or `getProjectAssignmentCandidates` when `includeOrganizationAdmins` is set) with no filtering of the policy's `createdBy`/`metadata.owner` anywhere in the hook or in `PolicyDetailView.jsx`'s usage of it (line 400). Backend confirmed still absent too: `WorkflowTransitionService.transition()` (`vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflowTransition.service.js`) and `policy.controller.js`'s `transition` handler perform no `assignedTo === policy.createdBy` check anywhere before creating the `assigned`/`re-assign` WorkflowEntry. A policy author can still select themselves as reviewer and later approve their own policy.

title: `effectiveDate` accepts past dates with no minimum; `nextReviewDate` not validated against `effectiveDate` — `Yup.date().nullable()` only; backdated and inverted dates silently accepted; violates Clause 7.5
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyCreate.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Both Yup schemas use `Yup.date().nullable()` for `effectiveDate` and `nextReviewDate` with no `.min()` and no cross-field validation ensuring `nextReviewDate > effectiveDate`.
**Impact:** Backdated effective dates and inverted review schedules silently accepted. ISO 27001 Clause 7.5 document control requires accurate dates; incorrect dates in the policy register mislead auditors.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
`effectiveDate: Yup.date().min(new Date(), 'Must be today or future').nullable()`. `nextReviewDate: Yup.date().nullable().test('after-effective', 'Must be after effective date', function(val) { return !val || !this.parent.effectiveDate || val > new Date(this.parent.effectiveDate); })`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyCreate.jsx` is now a thin wrapper delegating to `PolicyEdit.jsx` (its own create/edit form logic no longer exists as a separate component). In `PolicyEdit.jsx:352-363` the Yup schema now has (comments cite PM-005): `effectiveDate: Yup.date().nullable().transform(...).min(new Date(), 'Effective date must be today or in the future')` and `nextReviewDate` carries a `.test('after-effective', ...)` cross-field check ensuring it is strictly after `effectiveDate`. A soft (non-blocking) warning for effective dates more than a year in the past is also implemented (line ~1080).

title: AI-generated policies can be saved active without mandatory review — 'Save to Policy Library' creates no review request, sets no `aiGenerated: true` flag, allows `status: 'active'` immediately; violates Clause 7.5.2
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyAIGenerator.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** 'Save to Policy Library' creates a policy with no `aiGenerated: true` flag and no automatic review request. AI-generated content goes directly to whichever status the user selects, including `active`.
**Impact:** Unreviewed AI content becomes official organizational policy. ISO 27001 Clause 7.5.2 requires documented review and approval. AI-generated policies are indistinguishable from manually-approved ones to an auditor.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `PolicyAIGenerator.jsx` `handleSave`: force `status: 'draft'` and `aiGenerated: true`. After save, auto-call `POST /api/policies/:id/submit-for-review`. In `policy.controller.js` `createPolicy`: persist `aiGenerated: body.aiGenerated || false` on the model.
fixEvidence: `PolicyAIGenerator.jsx`'s `handleSavePolicy` (line ~829) no longer sends a `status` at all — it only sends title/category/priority/frameworks/projectId to `policyService.aiCreatePolicy`. Server-side, the AI-generation-to-policy handler (`vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy-ai.controller.js` ~line 399-400) unconditionally sets `status: 'draft'` and `sourceType: 'ai_generated'` — the frontend cannot override either. Combined with the PM-001 fix (status can only reach `active` via the permission-gated `/transition` workflow, never directly), an AI-generated policy now always starts as `draft` and must pass through `assigned → under_review → active` like any manually authored policy. `sourceType`/`aiGenerated` provenance now also drives the AI badge (see PM-013).

title: `reviewFrequency` not auto-connected to `nextReviewDate` calculation — fields independent; authors manually compute review dates; incorrect or missing `nextReviewDate` is a common ISO audit finding; violates Clause 9.1
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyCreate.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `reviewFrequency` (annual/biannual/quarterly) and `nextReviewDate` are independent form fields. No `onChange` handler on `reviewFrequency` computes and populates `nextReviewDate`.
**Impact:** Authors must manually compute review dates. Incorrect `nextReviewDate` values are a common ISO 27001 audit finding and trigger false overdue alerts in management dashboards.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `handleFrequencyChange = (freq) => { const months = {annual:12,biannual:6,quarterly:3}[freq]; if (months) { const d = new Date(); d.setMonth(d.getMonth()+months); formik.setFieldValue('nextReviewDate', d.toISOString().split('T')[0]); } formik.setFieldValue('reviewFrequency', freq); };`. Wire to `reviewFrequency` select `onChange`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyEdit.jsx:766-799` (comments cite PM-007) implements a `reviewFrequency`→day-offset map and auto-fills `nextReviewDate` whenever `effectiveDate` or `reviewFrequency` changes and the field is still empty, plus an explicit 'Calculate' button (line ~1362) that sets `nextReviewDate = effectiveDate + reviewFrequency` on demand. `PolicyCreate.jsx` now just delegates to `PolicyEdit.jsx`, which is the live create/edit form.

title: Review deadline accepts past dates — deadline `Input` has no `min` attribute and no client-side validation; past deadlines create immediately-overdue reviews; inflates overdue count from creation moment
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`
**Root Cause:** The deadline `Input` has no `min` attribute and the Yup schema has no `.min(new Date())` validation. Past deadlines create immediately-overdue reviews from the moment of creation.
**Impact:** Overdue review count inflated from creation. Reviewers receive escalation notifications for reviews never realistically scheduled. Management overdue reports are misleading.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add to deadline Input: `min={new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]}`. Add to Yup schema: `deadline: Yup.date().min(new Date(), 'Deadline must be in the future').required('Deadline is required')`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The deadline field now lives in `PolicyDetailView.jsx`'s 'Assign Reviewer' modal, not `PolicyEdit.jsx` — assigning a reviewer/deadline is a workflow-transition action, not a general policy edit. | `PolicyDetailView.jsx` (comments explicitly cite PM-008 at lines 300, 402, 873, 1159, 2487): the deadline field defaults to today+7 days, is refreshed to a valid future default every time the assign modal opens, and is blocked client-side from being set in the past with an inline error flag. Server-side, `policy.validation.js:92-114`'s `transition` validator (used by `POST /policies/:policyId/transition`, the endpoint that now carries the `deadline`) rejects any deadline `<= new Date()` via a `.custom()` check (tagged 'PM-UX-03' — the same fix originally requested here and in PM-053).

title: No policy register export (CSV/Excel) — `PolicyList.jsx` has no Export Register button; auditor requesting a structured policy list receives no machine-readable output; violates Clause 7.5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyList.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyDashboard.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Backend `GET /api/policies/export` is implemented and returns a valid CSV. Neither `PolicyList.jsx` nor `PolicyDashboard.jsx` has a button calling this endpoint.
**Impact:** ISO 27001 Clause 7.5.3 requires document availability. Auditors requesting a structured policy register receive no machine-readable output and must screenshot or manually copy table data.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `PolicyList.jsx` action bar: `<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => window.open('/api/policies/export?format=csv', '_blank')}><Download className="w-4 h-4 mr-2" />Export Register</Button>`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyList.jsx:663` implements an Export Register action (comment cites PM-010) calling the backend `GET /policies/export?format=csv` endpoint (`policy.controller.js:322-460`, `exportPolicies`), which now also carries the PM-036 field-name fixes and PM-L03 reviewer-name resolution.

title: `FrameworkMapping` shows aggregate coverage % but no drill-down to uncovered controls — 73% progress bar with no link to the missing 27% of Annex A controls; violates Clause 6.1.3 SoA requirement
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/FrameworkMapping.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Coverage shown as a progress bar with no click handler. No UI to list which controls have no mapped policy. Users see "73%" with no actionable breakdown of the gap.
**Impact:** ISO 27001 Clause 6.1.3 SoA requires tracking all controls. A 27% gap is invisible — teams cannot identify or remediate uncovered controls from the UI.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setShowUncovered(true)}>Show {uncoveredCount} uncovered controls</Button>`. Compute `uncoveredControls = frameworkControls.filter(c => !mappedControlIds.has(c.id))`. Render in an expandable panel or modal.
fixEvidence: `FrameworkMapping.jsx:421-507` now renders a 'Coverage Gaps Detected' banner with a badge count and a 'View Details' button that opens a drawer (`isGapsOpen`/`onGapsOpen`) listing each gap's domain, coverage %, and the specific missing items, sourced from `mappingData.data.coverageGaps` returned by the backend.

title: Review deadline not shown in `ReviewDetail` action screen — visible in `ReviewDashboard` list but absent from the actual action screen; reviewer loses urgency context when acting; violates Clause 9.1
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/ReviewDetail.jsx` **Root Cause:** `review.deadline` is in the fetched review object but not rendered anywhere in `ReviewDetail.jsx`. Visible only in `ReviewDashboard` list. **Impact:** Reviewers lose urgency context when performing the actual review. Late approvals more likely, causing policy overdue status and inaccurate compliance reporting. **Claude Fix Prompt:** In `ReviewDetail.jsx` header: `{review.deadline &&
Due {formatDate(review.deadline)}
}`.
fixEvidence: `ReviewDetail.jsx:247-253` extracts `reviewDeadline` from the workflow-history assignment entry, and renders it prominently both in the metadata row (lines 803-817, colored red when `daysUntil(reviewDeadline) < 3`) and in a dedicated 'Next Review / Overdue' card (lines 850-904) showing the exact date and days remaining/overdue.

title: No visual differentiation between AI-generated and manually authored policies — no badge, no `aiGenerated` flag, no filter in `PolicyList`; auditor sampling policies unknowingly selects unreviewed AI draft as evidence; violates Clause 7.5.2
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyList.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyDetailView.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `PolicyList.jsx` renders all policies identically — no badge or indicator for `aiGenerated: true`. The flag is also never set on creation (see PM-006).
**Impact:** Auditors sampling policies unknowingly select unreviewed AI drafts as evidence. ISO 27001 Clause 7.5.2 requires knowing the authoring method of each document.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `PolicyList.jsx` policy row: `{policy.aiGenerated && <Badge variant="outline" className="text-xs"><Sparkles className="w-3 h-3 mr-1" />AI</Badge>}`. Add filter chip for AI-generated in the filter bar.
fixEvidence: `policy.repository.js:87` persists `sourceType` ('ai_generated' | 'manual' | etc., comment cites PM-013). `PolicyList.jsx:205,534,1377` adds a `sourceType` filter param and renders an 'AI' badge on AI-generated policies that have not yet been approved. `PolicyDetailView.jsx:1418` renders the same AI-origin badge in the detail header (comment: 'auditors must know this was machine-generated').

title: Backend `checkCompliance` returns `Math.floor(Math.random() * 30) + 70` — TODO comment "Implement actual compliance checking logic"; `PolicyDashboard` and `PolicyComplianceDashboard` display fabricated scores that change every page load; violates ISO/IEC 27007:2019 §6.3.2
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** `checkCompliance` body: `return Math.floor(Math.random() * 30) + 70` with TODO comment. Score changes on every page load. Both dashboards display this fabricated value.
**Impact:** Management review reports and certification evidence containing dashboard screenshots contain fabricated metrics. Major nonconformity under ISO 27001 Clause 9.1 — immediate audit failure.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Replace `checkCompliance` body: `const mappings = await PolicyControlMapping.find({organizationId, policyId: {$in: activePolicyIds}}); const coveredControls = new Set(mappings.map(m => String(m.controlId))); const total = await FrameworkControl.countDocuments({frameworkId: {$in: activeFrameworkIds}}); return total > 0 ? Math.round((coveredControls.size / total) * 100) : 0;`.
fixEvidence: No `Math.random` found anywhere in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/`. `checkCompliance` no longer exists — replaced by `PolicyService.getComplianceScore()` (`policy.service.js:295-325`), a real weighted calculation over `PolicyControlMapping` records (`WEIGHTS = {full:1, partial:0.5, planned:0.25, not_applicable:0}`, `score = round((weighted/mappings.length)*100)`), plus `getComplianceGaps()` and `getComplianceTrends()` (real monthly snapshots built from mapping history). Org-level `PolicyRepository.dashboardStats()`/`frameworkMappingStats()` use the equivalent real aggregate formula. Frontend `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx:233` even documents the exact methodology in a tooltip (see PM-017).

title: View count increment not awaited — `Policy.findOneAndUpdate` for `viewCount`/`lastViewedAt` missing `await` in `policyController.js` line 630; concurrent access loses view counts; dashboard statistics unreliable
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** Line ~630: `Policy.findOneAndUpdate({_id}, {$inc:{viewCount:1}, $set:{lastViewedAt: new Date()}})` missing `await`. Promise abandoned under concurrent access.
**Impact:** View count statistics unreliable. Actual policy access frequency cannot be audited. `lastViewedAt` timestamps frequently incorrect.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `await`: `try { await Policy.findOneAndUpdate({_id: id}, {$inc:{viewCount:1}, $set:{lastViewedAt: new Date()}}); } catch(e) { /* non-critical — do not block response */ }`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The view-count increment now lives in `policy.repository.js`'s `incrementViewCount()`, called from `policy.controller.js`'s `getById` (`await PolicyRepository.incrementViewCount(policy.policyId)`), not inline in the controller. | `policy.repository.js:326-334`: `async incrementViewCount(policyId) { try { await Policy.updateOne({policyId, isLatest: true}, {$inc:{viewCount:1}, $set:{lastAccessedAt: new Date()}}); } catch (e) { /* non-critical */ } }` — the update is now properly awaited inside a try/catch exactly as prescribed.

title: Review delegation notification not sent — `delegateReview` in `policyController.js` line 5186 has TODO "Send notification to new reviewer"; delegated reviewers may miss review deadlines
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** `delegateReview` line ~5186 has TODO: "Send notification to new reviewer". No notification call present.
**Impact:** Delegated reviewers miss assignments. Policies assigned for delegation go overdue. Review completion rates underreported.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
After updating the review record: `await NotificationService.send({ userId: newReviewerId, type: 'review_delegated', title: 'Policy Review Assigned to You', body: \`\${policy.title} requires your review by \${formatDate(review.deadline)}\`, link: \`/policy-management/reviews/\${reviewId}\` });`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The standalone `delegateReview` endpoint/TODO no longer exists — delegation (re-assignment) is now handled generically by `POST /policies/:policyId/transition` with `targetState: 're-assign'`, the same endpoint used for the initial assignment. | `workflowTransition.service.js:206-247`: `WorkflowTransitionService.transition()` now unconditionally dispatches a notification whenever `targetState` is `'assigned'` or `'re-assign'` and `opts.assignedTo` is set — `notificationService.dispatch({ targetUserId: opts.assignedTo, notificationType: targetState === 're-assign' ? 'task_reassigned' : 'task_assigned', ... navigateTo: '/policy-management/${entityId}', dueDate: opts.deadline, ... })`. This covers the policy re-assign/delegate case (and every other entity type using the shared workflow engine), so the delegated reviewer is now notified with a deep link and due date.

title: Template-based PDF/DOCX export not implemented — TODO comments at lines 3504 and 3510 in `policyController.js`; current export uses basic HTML parsing with hardcoded margins; no template customization available
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** Lines ~3504 and ~3510: both PDF and DOCX export handlers return `res.status(501)` with TODO comments.
**Impact:** Enterprise customers receive 501 errors when attempting formal policy export. Distribution in standard document formats impossible.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
`npm install puppeteer`. PDF handler: `const browser = await puppeteer.launch({args:['--no-sandbox']}); const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.setContent(policyHtml, {waitUntil:'networkidle0'}); const pdf = await page.pdf({format:'A4', printBackground:true}); await browser.close(); res.set({'Content-Type':'application/pdf','Content-Disposition':\`attachment; filename="\${policy.title}.pdf"\`}); res.send(pdf);`.
fixEvidence: `policy.controller.js`'s `queueExport` (~line 1186-1311+) now fully implements PDF via `pdfkit` (custom markdown-to-PDF renderer: `renderMarkdownToPDF`/`renderTableToPDF`, handles headings/lists/tables/blockquotes/code blocks with real pagination) and DOCX via the real OOXML `docx` package (`policy-docx.service.js`'s `generatePolicyDocx`). No `res.status(501)` remains for either format — both formats plus `markdown`, `json`, and `csv` are fully supported (`SUPPORTED = ['pdf','docx','markdown','json','csv']`).

title: Org-level compliance-score endpoint has no cross-org ownership check — `GET /:id/compliance-score` and `POST /:id/recalculate-compliance-score` accept an arbitrary target org ID with no `req.params.id === req.orgId` guard; cross-tenant compliance data disclosure (IDOR)
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/organization/organization.controller.js` (`getComplianceScore` line 353; `recalculateComplianceScore` line 438, which just delegates to `getComplianceScore`); `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/organization/organization.routes.js:29-30`
**Root Cause:** The route chain is `authenticate` → `augmentPermissionsWithAnyProjectGrant()` → `requirePermission('policy.read')` → `getComplianceScore`. `orgId = req.params.id` is used directly to build the `PolicyControlMapping` query filter with no check that `req.params.id` equals `req.orgId` (the caller's own organization). The controller's own code comment confirms this is known and deliberately deferred: `// PLAC-006: membership-verified against the caller's own org (req.orgId) — note this endpoint separately has no check that req.params.id (the target org) matches the caller's own org at all; that's a pre-existing, unrelated cross-org IDOR out of scope for this fix and flagged separately, not silently expanded into here.` Re-verified directly against current code 2026-08-27: `requirePermission('policy.read')` only confirms the caller holds `policy.read` somewhere (their own org context), never that `req.params.id` matches `req.orgId`; `resolveProjectScope(req, projectId)` (line 369) likewise only narrows within whatever `organizationId` filter was already set from the unchecked `req.params.id`.
**Impact:** Any authenticated user holding `policy.read` in their own organization can substitute an arbitrary org ID as `:id` and read that other organization's policy-compliance breakdown — aggregate score, `totalMappings`, `totalPolicies`, and (with `?includeBreakdown=true`) a full per-framework/per-control coverage-level breakdown. `recalculateComplianceScore` inherits the identical gap since it calls `exports.getComplianceScore(req, res)` directly. This is a cross-tenant data-disclosure (IDOR) in a genuinely multi-tenant platform whose entire access model otherwise depends on org-scoping.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/organization/organization.controller.js — exports.getComplianceScore (line 353).

Immediately after `const orgId = req.params.id;`, add:
  if (String(orgId) !== String(req.orgId)) {
    throw AppError.forbidden('Cannot access another organization\'s compliance data');
  }
(match the AppError helper style already used elsewhere in this file).

recalculateComplianceScore (line 438) delegates directly to getComplianceScore(req, res),
so fixing the one function covers both routes — verify with a test rather than assuming.

Add a regression test in organization.controller.test.js: authenticate as a user in org A
with policy.read, call GET /organizations/{orgB_id}/compliance-score, assert 403.
```

title: AI generation/refinement credit reservation commits at task-submission time, not completion — if the client never re-polls status after a Python-side failure, `metering.reverse()` is never invoked and consumed AI quota/credits are never released; no background reconciliation job exists for these two operations
requirement: Billing/entitlement integrity — real customer AI-credit spend correctness
description:
**Files:** `policy-ai.controller.js` (`generate`, `getGenerationStatus`, `refineGeneration`, `getRefinementStatus`), `policy-ai-metering.service.js`, `balance.service.js`
**Root Cause:** `generate` calls `metering.begin()` then, as soon as the Python service *accepts* the job for async processing (not once it actually succeeds), calls `metering.accept()` (line 124) — this commits the reserved quota-key + AI-credit cost from `reservedValue` into `usedValue` in `EntitlementBalance`. The corresponding release only happens inside `getGenerationStatus` (line 254/267, `metering.reverse()`), which fires ONLY when the client polls again and observes `pyStatus === 'failed'` or a late `cache_hit`. `refineGeneration`/`getRefinementStatus` follow the identical commit-then-client-driven-reverse pattern (lines 331 and 385). If the browser tab is closed, the user navigates away, or the network drops before the client polls to a terminal state, the committed credits/quota are never released — there is no backend path that detects 'this generation actually failed/was abandoned in Python' independent of a client poll. Verified there is no mitigating background job: `balance.service.js`'s `expireStaleReservations()` (wired into `subscription-term.worker.js:26`) only reclaims reservations that were NEVER finalized (no commit or cancel event at all) — it explicitly does not touch a reservation that was already committed via `accept()`, which is exactly the state these generations are in. Repo-wide search confirms no cron/BullMQ job anywhere reconciles stuck/failed `PolicyAIGeneration` records against their metering charge, and `listGenerations` (line 158-162) is a plain find-and-return with no background stuck-record sync — unlike the sibling AI Reader flow (`policy-reader.controller.js`), whose `listDocuments` DOES opportunistically re-check and reverse billing for documents stuck in `processing`/`uploaded` when a user happens to revisit the document list (see PM-050's partial mitigation) — no equivalent exists for `generate`/`refine` at all.
**Impact:** A meaningful share of failed or abandoned AI policy generations/refinements will permanently consume the organization's annual AI-credit and generation-count entitlements with zero corresponding value delivered and zero visibility — this directly erodes the correctness of the same shared `balance.service.js` ledger other QA agents (Billing_Plans, Evidence_Management, AI_Assistant) already depend on for accurate spend tracking. Customers on a metered/capped AI-credit plan can be pushed toward false quota-exhaustion errors (`AI_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED`) by generations that never actually completed.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
1. Add a scheduled reconciliation job (BullMQ or a new worker alongside subscription-term.worker.js)
   that queries PolicyAIGeneration/refinements with status:'processing' and updatedAt older than a
   timeout (e.g. 20 minutes), re-checks their real status via AIProxy.getGenerationStatus(taskId),
   and — if Python reports 'failed' or the taskId is unknown/expired — calls
   metering.reverse({orgId, projectId, operation, resourceId}) and marks the local record 'failed',
   exactly mirroring the logic already in policy-ai.controller.js's getGenerationStatus failure branch.

2. Apply the identical reconciliation to refinement entries (operation: 'refinement').

3. Alternatively/additionally, give listGenerations the same opportunistic stuck-record re-check
   pattern policy-reader.controller.js's listDocuments already implements, as an interim mitigation
   until the scheduled job ships.
```

title: The exact same control disagrees between /policy-management and /grc-framework, root-caused by PM-060
description:
The UCL side does status-filtering correctly: resource-hydration.util.js:120-124 filters policy docs by status:'active' before they count; client-compliance-sync.service.js:2645-2657 (recomputeControlCoverage) only scores the policy dimension as 100 when a validated, ACTIVE Policy doc resolves. The policy-management side does not (see PM-060).

Auditor-facing breakage: for a control mapped only to a still-draft policy, /policy-management's FrameworkMapping/PolicyComplianceDashboard will show it as covered/'Full', while /grc-framework's UCL-fed coverage view correctly shows it as gap/uncovered. An auditor who cross-checks the same control across the two modules will find a direct contradiction with no reconciliation note anywhere in either UI, and no way to tell which screen to trust (the UCL one is the one that's actually right).

title: Policy reject/needs-revision/archive transitions require no justification — `policy` has no `commentRequiredTransitions` entry in `featureWorkflows.js`, unlike `evidence`'s equivalent transitions
description:
**Checklist row:** §4.5 — Justification required on destructive/terminal actions: closing, revoking, or rejecting a record requires a mandatory note/reason, not a bare status flip.
**Files:** `featureWorkflows.js:31-45` (the `policy` workflow definition) has no `commentRequiredTransitions` array at all. Compare `featureWorkflows.js:104-124` (the `evidence` definition, sitting immediately below it), which defines `commentRequiredTransitions: [['under_review', 'needs_revision'], ['under_review', 'closed']]` with an explicit code comment: "Reject/request-revision and Approve must both carry a substantive justification ... an approval with no real justification is a challengeable audit trail under ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9 just as much as an unexplained rejection." `WorkflowTransitionService._getDefinition()` (`workflowTransition.service.js:378-417`) builds `def.transitionDefs` exclusively from each entity type's `commentRequiredTransitions` array; since policy's is absent, `def.transitionDefs` is empty for policy and `transitionDef?.commentRequired` (checked at `workflowTransition.service.js:99-106`) is never true for any policy transition.
**Root Cause:** The `commentRequiredTransitions` design pattern was applied to `evidence` but never carried over to `policy` when the shared `WorkflowTransitionService` was built — an omission, not a deliberate choice (nothing in the codebase or commit comments suggests policy was intentionally exempted).
**Impact:** `POST /policies/:policyId/transition` accepts `under_review → rejected`, `under_review → needs_revision`, and `active → archived` (as well as `expired → archived`) with no `comment`/note of any length. A reviewer can reject a policy, send it back for revision, or an admin can archive a live, in-force policy with zero recorded rationale. This is the same class of gap PM-003 already flags for pre-approval checklist enforcement, but here it's the *decision* itself (why was this rejected / why was this archived) that leaves no audit trail — directly undermining ISO 27001 Clause 7.5's documented-decision requirement and Annex A.5.33 (protection of records) for exactly the terminal/destructive actions the checklist calls out by name.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-backend/src/core/constants/featureWorkflows.js`, add to the `policy` workflow definition (alongside `transitions`): `commentRequiredTransitions: [['under_review', 'rejected'], ['under_review', 'needs_revision'], ['active', 'archived'], ['expired', 'archived']]`. No change needed in `workflowTransition.service.js` — `_getDefinition()` already turns this array into `transitionDefs` with `commentRequired: true`, and the existing `MIN_COMMENT_LENGTH = 25` check at line ~100 will then apply automatically. Update `PolicyDetailView.jsx`'s `handleArchive` and any reject/needs-revision UI to collect and pass a `comment` in the `POST /transition` body before submitting, consistent with how `ReviewDetail.jsx` already collects a comment for its own actions.

title: `ai_policy_generator_python` accepts every request from `vibrantix-backend` with zero authentication — no `X-Internal-Token` (or any header at all) is sent, and the FastAPI service's only middleware is CORS + correlation-ID logging
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A.8.20 (network security) / A.8.26 (application security requirements)
description:
**Checklist row:** §10.2 — Internal microservice auth: any service-to-service call uses `X-Internal-Token`, not an unauthenticated internal route.
**Files:** `policy-ai-proxy.service.js`'s three request helpers all build their outgoing `headers` with no auth field: the JSON path (`_request`, line 114-116) sends only `{'Content-Type': 'application/json'}`; the multipart path (`_requestFormData`, line 179) sends `{}`; the streaming/download path (line 247-248) sends `headers: {}`. A repo-wide grep for `X-Internal-Token`/`internalToken`/`INTERNAL_TOKEN` anywhere in this file returns nothing. On the receiving side, `ai_policy_generator_python/app/main.py:63-101` registers exactly two middlewares — `CORSMiddleware` and a request-correlation/logging middleware (`correlation_and_request_logging`) — neither performs any authentication or token check; there is no `Depends()`-based auth dependency on any route either (confirmed: no `X-Internal-Token`/token-verification hit anywhere under `ai_policy_generator_python/app/`).
**Root Cause:** Unlike the platform's other internal microservices (vendor-service, risk-management-service, trust-vault-service, vciso-service, assistant-service, connector-service — all of which the RBAC/security QA agents confirm enforce `X-Internal-Token` on their internal routes), this Python service was never brought into that same internal-auth convention.
**Impact:** Any actor able to reach this service's network address (docker-compose default networking, a misconfigured ingress, or lateral movement from another compromised container) can call every one of its routes directly — trigger AI policy generation/refinement, consume LLM cost/quota, or invoke whatever data-bearing endpoints it exposes — completely bypassing `vibrantix-backend`'s `authenticate`/`requirePermission`/PLAC/entitlement-reservation layers this checklist run confirmed are otherwise well-enforced (`policy-ai.routes.js`). Since the service has no auth concept at all, it also has no way to distinguish or scope requests by organization on its own — whatever org/project context arrives in the request body is trusted as-is.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `policy-ai-proxy.service.js`, add `'X-Internal-Token': process.env.AI_POLICY_GENERATOR_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to the `headers` object in all three request helpers (`_request` line 114, `_requestFormData` line 179, and the streaming call at line 247). In `ai_policy_generator_python/app/main.py`, add a FastAPI dependency (e.g. `verify_internal_token` checking `request.headers.get('x-internal-token')` against the same env var) applied via `dependencies=[Depends(verify_internal_token)]` on the app or router level (excluding `/health`, `/metrics`, `/api/openapi.json`), matching the `X-Internal-Token` convention already used by every other internal microservice on this platform.
